svg.title: Who Touches the Deductible and the Claim Check
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-deductible-and-claim-check-parties; chapter number: 11; title: Who Touches the Deductible and the Claim Check; subtitle: The parties a contractor coordinates to get paid legally; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Restoration or Roofing Contractor; headcount: Not stated by the speakers; focus: Collect the deductible from the homeowner and never bill the carrier a number the client was never charged, which Chad Michael calls a felony in every state; spokes: role: Homeowner; type: Deductible payer; kpi: 2% on a $500,000 dwelling is $10,000, owed on a $12,000 loss or a total loss (Anne Pullen); role: Carrier; type: Insurer; kpi: Withholds the deductible from the payout; subrogation refunded it in about 6 months (Collision Crash Course); role: Mortgage Loss Draft Department; type: Lender; kpi: Under $10,000 endorsed with no holdback; over $10,000 goes to inspection (Richard Levisee); role: Assignment Counsel; type: Legal; kpi: Confirm a true assignment, not a direction to pay, signed by every named insured (Butler Legal); caption: A roofer who waives or eats the deductible is usually inflating the estimate or cutting roof quality.; assumptions note: Legal deductible coverage per Chad Michael means mining ACV-only other-structures money or subcontracting trades back to the owner. The lender threshold is from one sample mortgage package.; note: Attributed to Anne Pullen, Restoration Roofing, Collision Crash Course, Richard Levisee, Butler Legal, Integrity Roofing and Painting and Chad Michael.
